key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast perovskite photoluminescence degradation on unseen samples, enabling faster stability assessment from time-series spectra.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to shorten accelerated-aging campaigns for perovskite solar materials while preserving interpretability of the stability drivers.
method: Collected 86k+ PL spectra from 167 metal halide perovskite samples under heat and light stress.
Featurized spectra with a physics-informed model to encode degradation-relevant information.
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL intensity for unseen materials and compositions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a diverse dataset of 167 samples and >86,000 spectra, with the proposed model generalizing across material groups and outperforming baseline benchmarks.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the breadth and quality of the training dataset, so deployment on new perovskite chemistries or stress conditions should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
